scope: Data the Explorer research mode collects and sends to the apgi-api research contract (contracts/explorer-research-v1.json) once research is enabled. DRAFT for human review: it does not enable research, is not legal advice, and has not been checked against App Store Connect nutrition-label answers.
enablement_blockers: A named reviewer approves this inventory (set reviewer, reviewed_at, approved).

The approved manifest replaces APGI-Explorer/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy and APGI-Explorer-iOS/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy, release-hashes.json is updated, and privacy_manifest_sha256 here is set to the new hash.
collected_data_types_declared is set to true only after that replacement.
Consent texts are approved (S1-PRV-06) so the privacy policy view and the consent texts agree.
Only then may ExplorerBuildApproval.researchApproved become true (scripts/check_explorer_contracts.py enforces the ordering).

inventory.data: Username and, only if the participant registers with it, an email address
inventory.apple_type: NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeEmailAddress (email); username is covered by User ID
inventory.when: Account sign-in or registration inside the research flow
inventory.notes: Email is optional in the flow. The participant record itself is created with an empty body (pseudonymous).

inventory.data: Participant ID, participant-session ID and the account's user ID
inventory.notes: The shipped manifest already declares User ID as not linked; research makes it linked.

inventory.data: Answer value for each of the 35 items, the previous value when an answer changes, and the instrument hash
inventory.when: Each answer, uploaded through the outbox
inventory.notes: Whether self-reported attentional/psychological answers count as Health data is an open question below.
The shipped manifest declares Product Interaction as not linked; research makes it linked.

inventory.data: Which of the four consent purposes were granted or withdrawn, with versions and timestamps

not_collected: Personal profiles, personal journals and QuizSession data (never read into the research outbox; enforced by CI).
Names, demographics, location, contacts, photos, advertising identifiers or device identifiers.
Sensor data. Authentication tokens live only in the device-local Keychain and are not collected data.
Any data used for tracking; NSPrivacyTracking stays false with no tracking domains.
withdrawal: Revoking research consent stops uploads (server returns 403) and the app purges the local outbox for the session (ResearchWorkflow.withdraw). Deleting data already held by the server is a server-side erasure process (apgi-api deletion tasks) and must be described in the privacy policy before release.
open_questions: Do self-reported attentional/psychological questionnaire answers need the Health data type in the App Store privacy label, and what do the research ethics approvals say about special-category data?
Do apgi-api request logs retain IP address or device metadata? If so, add the relevant data types (Device ID/other) and a retention statement.
Which retention period applies to raw events, and is it stated in the consent texts?
Is the optional email used for anything beyond account recovery (recontact is a separate consent purpose)?
Does the iOS manifest need identical content? APGI-Explorer-iOS/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy differs from the macOS manifest today.
